mismatches.name: bash/faq73-transformations.sh
mismatches.script:
# source: https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashFAQ/073 (Bash 4 / parameter transformation)
# desc: ^ ^^ , ,, and @Q @E @A @a transformations
string='hello, World!'
echo "${string^}"; echo "${string^^}"; echo "${string,}"; echo "${string,,}"
string=$'nice "day" isn\'t it?' ; echo "${string@Q}"
string='hello\tworld' ; echo "${string@E}"
string=hello ; echo "${string@A}"
a=(an array); echo "${a[@]@A}"
declare -ri i=3 ; echo "${i@A}"
echo "${string@a}"
echo "${a@a}" "${i@a}"

hello, world!
'nice "day" isn'\''t it?'
hello	world
string='hello'
declare -a a=([0]="an" [1]="array")
declare -ir i='3'

a ir

mismatches.name: bash/pbb-progress-bar.sh
mismatches.script:
# source: https://github.com/dylanaraps/pure-bash-bible#progress-bars
# desc: printf -v with dynamic width and ${prog// /-}
bar() {
    # Usage: bar 1 10
    #            ^----- Elapsed Percentage (0-100).
    #               ^-- Total length in chars.
    ((elapsed=$1*$2/100))

    # Create the bar with spaces.
    printf -v prog  "%${elapsed}s"
    printf -v total "%$(($2-elapsed))s"

    printf '%s\r' "[${prog// /-}${total}]"
}
for i in 0 10 55 100; do bar "$i" 10; echo; done | tr '\r' R

mismatches.name: bash/pbb-reverse-array-extdebug.sh
mismatches.desc: BASH_ARGV under extdebug (bible notes compat44 is needed in 5.0+)
mismatches.script:
# source: https://github.com/dylanaraps/pure-bash-bible#reverse-an-array
# desc: BASH_ARGV under extdebug (bible notes compat44 is needed in 5.0+)
reverse_array() {
    # Usage: reverse_array "array"
    shopt -s extdebug
    f()(printf '%s\n' "${BASH_ARGV[@]}"); f "$@"
    shopt -u extdebug
}

mismatches.name: bash/pitfall-v-hash-key.sh
mismatches.script:
# source: https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashPitfalls#pf61 ([[ -v hash[$key] ]])
# desc: [[ -v 'hash[$key]' ]] single-quoted form, and ${hash[$key]} membership
declare -A hash=([a]=1 ['x y']=2)
for key in a 'x y' missing; do
  if [[ -v 'hash[$key]' ]]; then echo "$key: set"; else echo "$key: unset"; fi
  if [[ ${hash[$key]} ]]; then echo "$key: nonempty"; fi
done

mismatches.name: sed/gnu-doubled-words.sh
mismatches.desc: find doubled words on one line and across lines with \b \w \s
mismatches.script:
# source: https://www.gnu.org/software/sed/manual/html_node/Text-search-across-multiple-lines.html
# desc: find doubled words on one line and across lines with \b \w \s
# tags: gnu-ext (\b, \w, \s)
printf 'It was the best of times,\nit was the worst of times,\nit was the the age of wisdom,\n' > dup1.txt
sed -En '/\b(\w+)\s+\1\b/{=;p}' dup1.txt
printf 'It was the best of times, it was the\nworst of times, it was the\nthe age of wisdom,\nit was the age of foolishness,\n' > dup2.txt
sed -En '{N; /\b(\w+)\s+\1\b/{=;p} ; D}' dup2.txt

bash.stdout:
3
it was the the age of wisdom,
3
worst of times, it was the
the age of wisdom,
